cases.databases_differ: A trigger that skips the change of a row exists on PostgreSQL and SQLite, where the rotation finds the row unchanged and returns the conflict of INT-48; on MySQL a trigger can only refuse the update, which every client reports as DRIVER (DIA-223, INT-60).

steps.reason: the function of the trigger that drops the update of the second row
steps.sql: CREATE FUNCTION rot_row_second() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN IF OLD.seq = 2 THEN RETURN NULL; END IF; RETURN NEW; END $$

steps.reason: the second row takes no update: PostgreSQL and SQLite drop it, so it changes no row, and MySQL, where a trigger cannot drop an update, refuses it

sql.mysql: CREATE TRIGGER rot_row_second BEFORE UPDATE ON rot_row FOR EACH ROW IF OLD.seq = 2 THEN SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000' SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'rot_row_second'; END IF
sql.postgres: CREATE TRIGGER rot_row_second BEFORE UPDATE ON rot_row FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION rot_row_second()
sql.sqlite: CREATE TRIGGER rot_row_second BEFORE UPDATE ON rot_row WHEN OLD.seq = 2 BEGIN SELECT RAISE(IGNORE); END

steps.reason: removes the trigger, so the same rotation has nothing in its way
